subject: Science
text: Describe the characteristics of living things. - Need water, food and air to survive - Grow, respond and reproduce

subject: Science
text: Recognise some broad groups of living things based on similarities and differences. - Plants (flowering, non-flowering) - Animals (amphibians, birds, fish, insects, mammals, reptiles) - Fungi (mould, mushroom, yeast) - Bacteria

subject: Science

text: Show an understanding that different living things have different life cycles. - Plants - Animals

subject: Science
text: Recognise that a cell is a basic unit of life.

subject: Science
text: Show an understanding that living things reproduce to ensure continuity of their kind and that many characteristics of an organism are passed on from parents to offspring.

subject: Science
text: Recognise the process of fertilisation in the sexual reproduction of humans.

subject: Science
text: Identify the human systems in the body and state their functions (digestive, respiratory, circulatory, skeletal and muscular).

subject: Science
text: Identify the parts in the human digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine and large intestine) and describe their functions.

subject: Science
text: Recognise that air is made up of gases such as nitrogen, carbon dioxide, oxygen and water vapour.

subject: Science
text: Identify the parts of the human respiratory (nose, windpipe, lungs) and circulatory systems (heart, blood, blood vessels) and describe their functions.

subject: Science
text: Recognise the integration of the different systems (digestive, respiratory and circulatory) in carrying out life processes.

subject: Science
text: Identify the parts of the human respiratory (nose, windpipe, lungs) and circulatory systems (heart, blood, blood vessels) and state their functions.

text: Identify the different parts of plants and state their functions. - Leaf - Stem - Root

text: Identify the parts of the plant transport system and describe their functions.

subject: Science
text: Recognise how water is transported from the roots to other parts of the plant and how food is transported from the leaves to other parts of the plant.

text: Recognise that an electric circuit consisting of an energy source (battery) and other circuit components (wire, bulb, switch) forms an electrical system.

text: Show an understanding that a closed circuit allows current to flow.

subject: Science
text: Identify electrical conductors and insulators.

subject: Science
text: State that a closed circuit allows current to flow.

subject: Science
text: Recognise that a magnet can exert a push or a pull.

subject: Science
text: Identify the characteristics of magnets. - Magnets can be made of iron or steel. - Magnets have two poles. A freely suspended bar magnet comes to rest pointing in a North-South direction. - Unlike poles attract and like poles repel. - Magnets attract magnetic materials.

subject: Science
text: Recognise uses of magnets in everyday objects.

subject: Science
text: Identify a force as a push or a pull.

subject: Science
text: Show an understanding of the effects of a force. - A force can move a stationary object. - A force can speed up, slow down or change the direction of motion. - A force can stop a moving object. - A force may change the shape of an object.

subject: Science
text: Recognise and give examples of the different types of forces. - Magnetic force - Gravitational force - Elastic spring force - Frictional force

subject: Science

subject: Science
text: Show an understanding of the effect on organisms when the environment becomes unfavourable (organisms adapt and survive; move to other places or die).

subject: Science
text: Show an understanding of the energy pathway from the Sun through living things and identify the roles of various organisms (producers, consumers, predators, prey) in a food chain and a food web.

subject: Science
text: Differentiate among organism, population and community. - An organism is a living thing. - A population is a group of organisms of the same kind, living and reproducing at a given place and time. - A community consists of many populations living together in a particular place.

subject: Science
text: Show an understanding that different habitats support different communities (garden, field, pond, seashore, tree, mangrove swamp).

text: Identify good and poor conductors of heat. - Good conductors: metals - Poor conductors: wood, plastics, air, rubber
